background_notes.justification: Smooth periodic inputs have rapidly decreasing Fourier coefficients. Multiplication by polynomial frequency factors, Airy phases and their time derivatives preserves that decay, locally uniformly in time. For R2, the phase-average bound follows from the integral triangle inequality. A bounded trilinear multiplier applied to rapidly decreasing sequences has rapidly decreasing output: for any nonnegative integer m, weight the absolutely convergent convolution by <k>^m<=C_m<a>^m<b>^m<c>^m and bound its weighted ell1 norm by the product of the three weighted ell1 norms. Thus the displayed R2 formula is well defined and smooth on these smooth inputs, also as the limit of their Fourier truncations; no unproved rough-data extension is needed. Time integration preserves this smoothness. The zero Fourier coefficient of B and of R2 is zero; sums, time integrals and time differentiation preserve zero mean. Since z_n=f+F_n and Y_n=C_n+Q_n-(t-n*tau)W_n/tau, the asserted conditions follow. This supplies only regularity for applying the given identities, not any new quantitative project estimate.

Continuity implies that the difference quotient of a time primitive converges to its integrand, proving the derivative formulas. In accumulated concatenation the preceding increments are constant on the current step, and the new increment starts at zero, so no jump term is introduced.
